[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN, LSTM, and GRU)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sequential data processing is a fundamental requirement in modern machine learning tasks such as natural language processing, time-series forecasting, and speech recognition. Unlike traditional feedforward neural networks, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and their advanced variants (LSTMs and GRUs) are designed to handle sequential inputs by maintaining an internal state (memory) over time."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Standard Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard RNNs process sequences by iterating through sequence elements and maintaining a hidden state vector. At each time step t, the hidden state is updated using the current input and the previous hidden state."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Limitation: Standard RNNs suffer from vanishing and exploding gradient problems during backpropagation through time (BPTT), making it difficult to learn long-range dependencies."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"LSTMs were introduced to resolve the vanishing gradient issue of standard RNNs. They introduce a conveyor belt-like structure called the cell state, along with three gating mechanisms that regulate the flow of information: the forget gate, the input gate, and the output gate."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Forget Gate: Decides what information to discard from the cell state."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input Gate: Determines what new information to store in the cell state."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Output Gate: Controls what parts of the cell state will be outputted as the hidden state."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Gated Recurrent Units (GRU)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"GRUs are a simplified variant of LSTMs. They combine the cell state and hidden state, and use two gates: the update gate and the reset gate. GRUs have fewer parameters than LSTMs, which often results in faster training times while maintaining competitive performance."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementation Example using PyTorch"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical implementation of an LSTM-based sequence classifier using PyTorch."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class LSTMClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim, n_layers):
        super(LSTMClassifier, self).__init__()
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.n_layers = n_layers
        
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(input_dim, hidden_dim, n_layers, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        
    def forward(self, x):
        h0 = torch.zeros(self.n_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_dim).to(x.device)
        c0 = torch.zeros(self.n_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_dim).to(x.device)
        
        out, (hn, cn) = self.lstm(x, (h0, c0))
        out = self.fc(out[:, -1, :])
        return out

# Example instantiation
model = LSTMClassifier(input_dim=10, hidden_dim=20, output_dim=2, n_layers=2)
print(model)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Standard RNNs only for very short sequences or as a baseline."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use LSTMs when complex long-term dependencies must be captured accurately."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use GRUs as a computationally efficient alternative to LSTMs when dataset sizes are moderate or training speed is a priority."}]
